summary: Trojanized jQuery drop-in with XOR-obfuscated payload executed via Function constructor
details: scdn-jquery ships libs/18.2.0.js, which is headed with a fake 'jQuery v18.2.0' banner (a version jQuery has never released) and prepends a self-executing IIFE that base64-decodes an opaque string, XOR-decrypts it with a 4-byte key taken from the decoded prefix, and executes the resulting source via `new Function(...)()`. The package name and content positioning ('scdn' + jQuery banner, published as a single CDN-style asset) are consistent with a jQuery CDN drop-in, so any site that includes this file via a script tag — or any consumer that loads it — runs the hidden decoded payload. The README (Chinese) states 'Internal test package, do not use.' Legitimate jQuery builds contain no such loader; the obfuscated executable payload inside a file whose cover identity is jQuery is a trojaned-library shape.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
